name: Find C, then C D E

steps.title: Two black keys, then three
steps.text: The black keys come in groups of two and three, over and over. That pattern is how you find your way around.
steps.line: Hi, I’m Rulin. Look at the keyboard. Can you spot the groups of two black keys? I’ll light them up.

steps.title: C lives beside the group of two
steps.text: C is the white key just to the left of each group of two black keys. Find it once and you can find every other note from it.
steps.line: This is C. It’s always just left of the two black keys. Press it and listen.
Press C. Nothing else counts yet.

steps.title: D and E
steps.text: D sits between the two black keys. E is the white key just to their right. C, D, E: three steps up.
steps.line: Now D and E, the two keys to the right of C. Listen to how they climb.
I’ll call a note, you press it.
Now the other way round. I’ll light a key, you tell me its name.
Your first tune: Hot Cross Buns, with only C, D and E. The next key lights up and the note name is under the staff. No clock. Take your time.
You found C, D and E and played a real tune on day one. Tomorrow we add the next four notes and a tune you’ll know.

steps.title: The group of three
steps.text: You found C beside the two black keys. The three black keys mark the next four notes. F sits just to their left.
steps.line: Find the three black keys. F is the white key just to their left. I’ll play it so you hear it.

steps.title: F, G, A, B
steps.text: After F come G, A and B, one white key each, and then you are back at C. Seven letters, then they repeat.
steps.line: F, G, A, B. Then C again. Listen to the whole climb from C to C.
Press the note I call. Use the black-key groups to find your way.
All seven now, mixed up.
I’ll light a key. Tell me which one it is.
A listening game. I play a few notes, you play them back.
Ode to Joy, with everything from C to G. Lights and names first, then the notation on its own, then from memory.
All seven white keys and a tune most people recognize. Next time we add the click and start playing in time.

steps.title: Counting to four
steps.text: Music moves in a steady beat. Most tunes here count in fours: 1 2 3 4, 1 2 3 4. A quarter note lasts one count. A half note lasts two.
steps.line: Listen to the click. Count 1 2 3 4 with it. The filled notes get one count, the hollow ones get two.

steps.title: Hearing the difference
steps.text: Here is the first line of Twinkle Twinkle. Every note is one count except the last, which holds for two.
steps.line: I’ll play the first line with the click. Count along and notice the held note at the end.
Play these back. Try to keep the gaps even.
Twinkle Twinkle with the click on. Hold the hollow notes for two counts. If you drift, that’s fine, just keep going.
That’s rhythm. Next lesson you’ll start reading notes off the staff instead of waiting for the lights.

steps.title: Five lines, four spaces
steps.text: Notes on the staff climb the way keys climb. The higher the note sits, the higher the key. Middle C sits on its own short line just below the staff.
steps.line: This is middle C on the staff. It hangs under the five lines on a little line of its own. The dot on the keyboard marks the same key.

steps.title: Up the staff, up the keys
steps.text: From middle C, each step up the staff (line to space, space to line) is the next white key: D, E, F, G.
steps.line: Watch the note climb and listen. Same steps on the keys: C, D, E, F, G.
Which key is this? Press it. The octave matters, so use the dot for middle C.
A new tune you haven’t seen the keys for: Mary Had a Little Lamb. Read it off the staff. Lights help this first time.
You just read music. Next lesson is the black keys, and a tune that needs one.

steps.title: Black keys have two names
steps.text: A sharp is the black key just right of a white key. A flat is the one just left. So the black key between A and B is both A sharp and B flat.
steps.line: The black keys: each one is a sharp of the key below it and a flat of the key above. Let me show you B flat, just left of B.
Press the black key I name. Think about which white key it sits next to.

steps.title: On the staff
steps.text: A sharp sign or a flat sign sits just before the note it changes.
steps.line: Here is B flat written down: a flat sign, then the note on the middle line.
Read these. Some have a sign, some don’t.
Happy Birthday. It counts in threes and it needs a B flat near the end. Lights first.
Sharps and flats done. Next time the left hand joins in with its own clef.

name: The bass clef and left hand

steps.title: A second staff for the left hand
steps.text: Lower notes get their own staff with a different clef, the bass clef. Middle C sits just above it on a short line. The keyboard shifts down an octave for this lesson.
steps.line: Same letters, lower sounds. Here is middle C on the bass staff, hanging over the top line.

steps.title: Down the staff, down the keys
steps.text: Going down from middle C: B, A, G, F, E, D, C. The bass staff shows them stepping down line by line.
steps.line: Watch the note step down and listen. Use your left hand for these.
Read these on the bass staff and press the key. Left hand.
Hot Cross Buns again, an octave down, left hand only. You know the tune, so the reading is the new part.
Both clefs read. Last lesson puts the two hands together.

steps.title: The grand staff
steps.text: Treble on top for the right hand, bass below for the left, joined by a brace. When two notes line up vertically, you play them at the same time.
steps.line: Here is Ode to Joy with one left-hand note at the start of each bar. When the notes stack, press them together.
A few notes on the grand staff. Which key?
Ode to Joy, both hands. The left hand only plays on the first beat of each bar. Lights for both hands first.
That’s the whole path. Everything here lives in Practice and the Songbook now, and the Studio writes down anything you play.
